5.156.m: Then, having [sprinkled] all the vessels beginning with the ladle in proper order, / he designated his own body in place of the sacrificial offering.

5.156.s:
nyāyaṃ tu devatāsthāne sa ācāryavidhānataḥ ..
grahaṇaṃ prokṣaṇaṃ caiva sūryāya tveti cottaram .. 22 ..
5.156.d:
न्यायं तु देवतास्थाने स आचार्यविधानतः ..
ग्रहणं प्रोक्षणं चैव सूर्याय त्वेति चोत्तरम् .. 22 ..
5.156.m: And in place of the deity, in accordance with the preceptor's rule, / [he performed] the taking up and the sprinkling, and afterwards [the offering] with 'To Sūrya [svāhā]'.

5.156.s:
ayaṃ ta idhma ātmeti japtvātha samidhaṃ tataḥ ..
agnisometi mantrābhyāṃ hutvā cājyāhutī tataḥ .. 23 ..
5.156.d:
अयं त इध्म आत्मेति जप्त्वाथ समिधं ततः ..
अग्निसोमेति मन्त्राभ्यां हुत्वा चाज्याहुती ततः .. 23 ..
5.156.m: Then, having recited 'This is thy firewood, thy self' over the kindling stick, / and then having offered two ghee oblations with the two mantras to Agni and Soma,

5.156.s:
kṛtvā vyāhṛtihomaṃ tu bhūrbhuvaḥ sveti bho dvijāḥ ..
ye te śateti mantrādyairhutvātraiva ca dāruṇam .. 24 ..
5.156.d:
कृत्वा व्याहृतिहोमं तु भूर्भुवः स्वेति भो द्विजाः ..
ये ते शतेति मन्त्राद्यैर्हुत्वात्रैव च दारुणम् .. 24 ..
5.156.m: having performed the homa of the sacred utterances, 'bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ', O brahmins, / and having offered here a dreadful [sacrifice] with mantras such as 'ye te śatam',

5.156.s:
āhvayāmāsa vahniṃ ca pratyakṣo bhava deva me ..
evaṃ mantreṇa kṛtvā taṃ saṃmukhaṃ jvalanaṃ tataḥ .. 25 ..
5.156.d:
आह्वयामास वह्निं च प्रत्यक्षो भव देव मे ..
एवं मन्त्रेण कृत्वा तं संमुखं ज्वलनं ततः .. 25 ..
5.156.m: he invoked the Fire: 'O god, become visible to me!' / Having thus turned the blazing fire toward himself with the mantra,

5.156.s:
kālīkarālikādyāśca saptajihvāśca yāḥ smṛtāḥ ..
tāsāmāhvānakaṃ kṛtvā tato dīpte havirbhuji .. 26 ..
5.156.d:
कालीकरालिकाद्याश्च सप्तजिह्वाश्च याः स्मृताः ..
तासामाह्वानकं कृत्वा ततो दीप्ते हविर्भुजि .. 26 ..
5.156.m: and having summoned those known as the seven tongues, Kālī, Karālikā, and the rest, / then, into the blazing devourer of oblations,

5.156.s:
juhāva ca sa māṃsāni svāni cotkṛttya śastrataḥ ..
lomabhyaḥ svāheti vidiśo digbhyo dattvā tataḥ param .. 27 ..
5.156.d:
जुहाव च स मांसानि स्वानि चोत्कृत्त्य शस्त्रतः ..
लोमभ्यः स्वाहेति विदिशो दिग्भ्यो दत्त्वा ततः परम् .. 27 ..
5.156.m: he cut off and offered pieces of his own flesh with a weapon; / and having offered to the intermediate directions and the directions with 'svāhā to the hairs', thereafter,

5.156.s:
agnaye sviṣṭakṛtaiti yāvadātmānamākṣipet ..
tāvaddhṛtaḥ sa sūryeṇa svahastena samaṃtataḥ .. 28 ..
5.156.d:
अग्नये स्विष्टकृतैति यावदात्मानमाक्षिपेत् ..
तावद्धृतः स सूर्येण स्वहस्तेन समंततः .. 28 ..
5.156.m: just as he was about to cast himself [into the fire] with 'To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt', / he was seized on all sides by Sūrya with his own hand.

5.156.s:
dhṛtaśca sādaraṃ tena mā vipra kuru sāhasam ..
nedṛgghomaḥ kṛtaḥ kvāpi kadācitkenaciddvija .. .. 29 ..
5.156.d:
धृतश्च सादरं तेन मा विप्र कुरु साहसम् ..
नेदृग्घोमः कृतः क्वापि कदाचित्केनचिद्द्विज .. .. 29 ..
5.156.m: And held respectfully by him, [he heard:] 'Do not commit such a reckless act, O brahmin! / Such a homa has never anywhere been performed by anyone, O twice-born!

5.156.s:
tuṣṭo'haṃ ca mahābhāga brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te ..
adeyamapi dāsyāmi yatte manasivartate .. 6.157.30 ..
5.156.d:
तुष्टोऽहं च महाभाग ब्रूहि किं करवाणि ते ..
अदेयमपि दास्यामि यत्ते मनसिवर्तते .. 6.157.30 ..
5.156.m: I am pleased, O fortunate one; tell me, what shall I do for you? / Even what should not be given I will give, whatever is in your mind.'

5.156.s:
.. puṣpa uvāca .. ..
yadi tuṣṭosi deveśa yadi deyo varo mama ..
taddeyaṃ guṭikāyugmaṃ yadarthaṃ prārthayāmyaham .. 31 ..
5.156.d:
.. पुष्प उवाच .. ..
यदि तुष्टोसि देवेश यदि देयो वरो मम ..
तद्देयं गुटिकायुग्मं यदर्थं प्रार्थयाम्यहम् .. 31 ..
5.156.m: Puṣpa said: / 'If you are pleased, O Lord of gods, if a boon is to be granted to me, / then let that pair of pills be given for the sake of which I pray.

5.156.s:
vaidiśe nagare cāsti maṇibhadro mahādhanī ..
kubjāṃgaḥ kṣatriyo deva jarāvalisamanvitaḥ .. 32 ..
5.156.d:
वैदिशे नगरे चास्ति मणिभद्रो महाधनी ..
कुब्जांगः क्षत्रियो देव जरावलिसमन्वितः .. 32 ..
5.156.m: In the city of Vaidiśa there is a very wealthy man, Maṇibhadra, / a kṣatriya whose limbs are hunchbacked, O god, and who is covered with wrinkles of old age,

5.156.s:
abrahmaṇyo mahānīcaḥ kīnāśo janadūṣitaḥ ..
dvayorekāṃ yadā vaktre sadā caiva karomyaham .. 33 ..
5.156.d:
अब्रह्मण्यो महानीचः कीनाशो जनदूषितः ..
द्वयोरेकां यदा वक्त्रे सदा चैव करोम्यहम् .. 33 ..
5.156.m: hostile to brahmins, vile, a miser, reviled by the people. / Whenever I put one of the two into my mouth,

5.156.s:
tadā me tādṛśaṃ rūpamavikalpaṃ bhavatviti ..
yadā punargṛhītvā tāṃ dvitīyāṃ prakṣipāmyaham .. 34 ..
5.156.d:
तदा मे तादृशं रूपमविकल्पं भवत्विति ..
यदा पुनर्गृहीत्वा तां द्वितीयां प्रक्षिपाम्यहम् .. 34 ..
5.156.m: may I assume an exact form just like his, without doubt; / and whenever I take and put in the second one,

5.156.s:
tataśca sahajaṃ rūpaṃ mama bhūyātsureśvara ..
vaidiśe nagare cāsti maṇibhadraḥ sureśvara .. 35 ..
5.156.d:
ततश्च सहजं रूपं मम भूयात्सुरेश्वर ..
वैदिशे नगरे चास्ति मणिभद्रः सुरेश्वर .. 35 ..
5.156.m: may my natural form return, O Lord of the gods. / Maṇibhadra is in the city of Vaidiśa, O Lord of the gods;

5.156.s:
aparaṃ tasya yatkiṃciddhanadhānyādikaṃ gṛhe ..
tatsarvaṃ viditaṃ me syāttathā deva prajāyatām.. 36 ..
5.156.d:
अपरं तस्य यत्किंचिद्धनधान्यादिकं गृहे ..
तत्सर्वं विदितं मे स्यात्तथा देव प्रजायताम्.. 36 ..
5.156.m: further, whatever wealth, grain, and the like is in his house, / let all that be known to me; may it come to be so, O god!

5.156.s:
kiṃ vānena bahūktena tasya mitrāṇi bāṃdhavāḥ ..
vyavahārāstathā sarve prakaṭāḥ syuḥ sadaiva hi .. 37 ..
5.156.d:
किं वानेन बहूक्तेन तस्य मित्राणि बांधवाः ..
व्यवहारास्तथा सर्वे प्रकटाः स्युः सदैव हि .. 37 ..
5.156.m: Or what need is there to say much? His friends, his kinsmen, / and all his affairs, let them always be completely open [to me].

5.156.s:
na kaścijjāyate tatra vikalpaḥ kasyacitkvacit ..
mama tasyādhama syāpi sarvakṛtyeṣu sarvadā .. 38 ..
5.156.d:
न कश्चिज्जायते तत्र विकल्पः कस्यचित्क्वचित् ..
मम तस्याधम स्यापि सर्वकृत्येषु सर्वदा .. 38 ..
5.156.m: Let no doubt arise anywhere in anyone / regarding me, or even regarding that wretched man, in all actions at all times.'

5.156.s:
.. bhāskara uvāca .. ..
gṛhāṇa tvaṃ mahābhāga guṭikādvitayaṃ śubham ..
śuklaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ca vaktrasthaṃ vibheda jananaṃ mahat .. 39 ..
5.156.d:
.. भास्कर उवाच .. ..
गृहाण त्वं महाभाग गुटिकाद्वितयं शुभम् ..
शुक्लं कृष्णं च वक्त्रस्थं विभेद जननं महत् .. 39 ..
5.156.m: Bhāskara said: / 'Receive, O fortunate one, the auspicious pair of pills, / white and black, which, placed in the mouth, produce a great transformation.

5.156.s:
śuklayā tasya rūpaṃ ca tava nūnaṃ bhaviṣyati ..
kṛṣṇayāpi punaḥ svaṃ ca saṃprāpsyasi mahādvija .. 6.157.40 ..
5.156.d:
शुक्लया तस्य रूपं च तव नूनं भविष्यति ..
कृष्णयापि पुनः स्वं च संप्राप्स्यसि महाद्विज .. 6.157.40 ..
5.156.m: By the white one, you will surely take his form; / and by the black one, you will regain your own, O great twice-born.'

5.156.s:
.. puṣpa uvāca .. ..
aparaṃ vada me deva saṃdehaṃ hṛdaye sthitam ..
yattvāṃ pṛcchāmi deveśa tava kīrtivivardhanam ..41..
5.156.d:
.. पुष्प उवाच .. ..
अपरं वद मे देव संदेहं हृदये स्थितम् ..
यत्त्वां पृच्छामि देवेश तव कीर्तिविवर्धनम् ..41..
5.156.m: Puṣpa said: / 'Tell me another thing, O god, a doubt that remains in my heart, / which I ask you, O Lord of the gods, increasing your glory.

5.156.s:
mayā śrutaṃ suraśreṣṭha saptamyāṃ sūryavāsare ..
yaste pradakṣiṇānāṃ ca kuryādaṣṭottaraṃ śatam ..
tasya tvaṃ tatkṣaṇādeva phalahastasya siddhidaḥ .. 42 ..
5.156.d:
मया श्रुतं सुरश्रेष्ठ सप्तम्यां सूर्यवासरे ..
यस्ते प्रदक्षिणानां च कुर्यादष्टोत्तरं शतम् ..
तस्य त्वं तत्क्षणादेव फलहस्तस्य सिद्धिदः .. 42 ..
5.156.m: I have heard, O best of gods, that on a Sunday of the seventh tithi, / whoever circumambulates you one hundred and eight times, / with fruit in hand, to him you grant fulfillment at that very moment,

5.156.s:
mūrkhasyāpi ca pāpasya sarvadoṣānvitasya ca ..
caturvedasya me kasmāttīrthayātrāparasya ca .. 43 ..
5.156.d:
मूर्खस्यापि च पापस्य सर्वदोषान्वितस्य च ..
चतुर्वेदस्य मे कस्मात्तीर्थयात्रापरस्य च .. 43 ..
5.156.m: even if he is a fool, a sinner, and possessed of all faults. / Why is it that to me, who know the four Vedas and am devoted to pilgrimages,

5.156.s: saptarātre gate tuṣṭo homa evaṃvidhe kṛte .. 44 ..
5.156.d: सप्तरात्रे गते तुष्टो होम एवंविधे कृते .. 44 ..
5.156.m: you were pleased only after seven nights had passed, when such a homa was performed?'

5.156.s:
.. śrīsūrya uvāca.. ..
tāmasena tu bhāvena tvavā sarvamidaṃ kṛtam..
tena sarvaṃ vṛthā jātaṃ tvayā sarvaṃ ca yatkṛtam .. 49 ..
yatkiṃcitkriyate vipra tāmasaṃ bhāvamāśritaiḥ ..
tatsarvaṃ jāyate vyarthaṃ kiṃ na vetti bhavā nidam .. 46 ..
evamuktvā tataḥ sūryastasya gātrāṇyupāspṛśat ..
khaṃḍitāni svahastena nirvraṇāni kṛtāni ca .. 47 ..
abravīcca punaḥ puṣpaṃ prasanna vadanaḥ sthitaḥ ..
anenaiva vidhānena yaḥ karoti kuśaṃḍikām .. 48 ..
somyabhāvaṃ samāśritya samidbhiścārkasaṃbhavaiḥ ..
tilākṣatairviśeṣeṇa homaṃ yastu samācaret .. 49 ..
chandaṛṣisamopetamekaṃ yāvatsahasrakam ..
tasya dāsyāmyahaṃ hṛtsthamadhikebhyo'dhikaṃ phalam ..6.157.5...
5.156.d:
.. श्रीसूर्य उवाच.. ..
तामसेन तु भावेन त्ववा सर्वमिदं कृतम्..
तेन सर्वं वृथा जातं त्वया सर्वं च यत्कृतम् .. 49 ..
यत्किंचित्क्रियते विप्र तामसं भावमाश्रितैः ..
तत्सर्वं जायते व्यर्थं किं न वेत्ति भवा निदम् .. 46 ..
एवमुक्त्वा ततः सूर्यस्तस्य गात्राण्युपास्पृशत् ..
खंडितानि स्वहस्तेन निर्व्रणानि कृतानि च .. 47 ..
अब्रवीच्च पुनः पुष्पं प्रसन्न वदनः स्थितः ..
अनेनैव विधानेन यः करोति कुशंडिकाम् .. 48 ..
सोम्यभावं समाश्रित्य समिद्भिश्चार्कसंभवैः ..
तिलाक्षतैर्विशेषेण होमं यस्तु समाचरेत् .. 49 ..
छन्दऋषिसमोपेतमेकं यावत्सहस्रकम् ..
तस्य दास्याम्यहं हृत्स्थमधिकेभ्योऽधिकं फलम् ..6.157.5...
5.156.m:
The glorious Sūrya said: / 'All this was done by you with a dark, ignorant disposition; / therefore, all that was done by you came to naught.
Whatever is done, O brahmin, by those who resort to an ignorant disposition, / all that becomes useless; do you not know this?
Having spoken thus, Sūrya touched his limbs / that had been cut, with his own hand, and made them free of wounds.
And standing with a gracious countenance, he spoke again to Puṣpa: / 'Whoever performs the kuśaṇḍikā rite according to this very procedure,
relying upon a gentle disposition, and performs homa especially with kindling sticks / from the arka plant, and with sesame and unbroken grains,
reciting the meter and seer, for up to one thousand [oblations], / to him I will grant the desire in his heart, a fruit greater than the greatest.'

5.156.s:
evamuktvā sahasrāṃśustatraivāṃ taradhīyata ..
dīpavallakṣito naiva kena mārgeṇa nirgataḥ .. 51 ..
5.156.d:
एवमुक्त्वा सहस्रांशुस्तत्रैवां तरधीयत ..
दीपवल्लक्षितो नैव केन मार्गेण निर्गतः .. 51 ..
5.156.m: Having spoken thus, the thousand-rayed sun disappeared right there; / like a lamp, it was not perceived by what path he departed.

5.156.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye sūryasakāśātpuṣpabrāhmaṇasya varalabdhivarṇanaṃnāma saptapañcāśaduttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 157 ..
5.156.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये सूर्यसकाशात्पुष्पब्राह्मणस्य वरलब्धिवर्णनंनाम सप्तपञ्चाशदुत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 157 ..
5.156.m: Thus ends the one hundred fifty-seventh chapter, entitled "The Description of the Brahmin Puṣpa's Attainment of a Boon from Sūrya," in the section on the majesty of the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [book] in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.157.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
puṣpo'pi guṭike labdhvā bhāskarādvāritaskarāt ..
cirādbhojanamāsādya prasthito vaidiśaṃ prati .. 1 ..
5.157.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
पुष्पोऽपि गुटिके लब्ध्वा भास्कराद्वारितस्करात् ..
चिराद्भोजनमासाद्य प्रस्थितो वैदिशं प्रति .. 1 ..
5.157.m: Sūta said: / Having obtained the two pills from Bhāskara, who draws up the waters, / and having eaten after a long time, Puṣpa set out toward Vaidiśa.

5.157.s:
tato vaidiśamāsādya sa puṣpo hṛṣṭamānasaḥ ..
śuklā tāṃ guṭikāṃ vaktre cakāradvijasattamāḥ .. 2 ..
5.157.d:
ततो वैदिशमासाद्य स पुष्पो हृष्टमानसः ..
शुक्ला तां गुटिकां वक्त्रे चकारद्विजसत्तमाः .. 2 ..
5.157.m: Then, having arrived at Vaidiśa, Puṣpa, with a glad heart, / placed that white pill into his mouth, O best of twice-born.

5.157.s:
maṇibhadrasamo jātastatkṣaṇādeva sa dvijaḥ ..
haṭṭamārgaṃ gate so'tha tasmingatvā'tha maṃdire ..
praviṣṭaḥ sahasā madhye prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā .. 3 ..
5.157.d:
मणिभद्रसमो जातस्तत्क्षणादेव स द्विजः ..
हट्टमार्गं गते सोऽथ तस्मिन्गत्वाऽथ मंदिरे ..
प्रविष्टः सहसा मध्ये प्रहृष्टेनांतरात्मना .. 3 ..
5.157.m: That twice-born became identical to Maṇibhadra at that very moment. / When the other went along the market road, he then went to the house, / and hastily entered inside with a delighted heart.

5.157.s:
tataścākārayāmāsa taṃ ṣaṃḍhaṃ dvāramāśritam ..
tasya dattvātha vastrāṇi paścātṣaṃḍhamuvāca saḥ .. 4 ..
5.157.d:
ततश्चाकारयामास तं षंढं द्वारमाश्रितम् ..
तस्य दत्त्वाथ वस्त्राणि पश्चात्षंढमुवाच सः .. 4 ..
5.157.m: Then he summoned that eunuch standing at the door; / having given him garments, he afterwards spoke to the eunuch:

5.157.s:
ṣaṃḍhakaścitpumānatra samyagveṣakaro hi saḥ ..
mama veṣaṃ samādhāya bhramate sakale pure .. 5 ..
5.157.d:
षंढकश्चित्पुमानत्र सम्यग्वेषकरो हि सः ..
मम वेषं समाधाय भ्रमते सकले पुरे .. 5 ..
5.157.m: 'Eunuch, there is a certain man here who is an expert at disguises; / having assumed my appearance, he wanders through the entire town.

5.157.s:
sāṃprataṃ madgṛhe so'tha lobhanāyāgamiṣyati ..
sa ca kṛtrima veṣeṇa niṣeddhavyastvayā hi saḥ ..
sa tatheti pratijñāya dvāradeśaṃ samāśritaḥ .. 6 ..
5.157.d:
सांप्रतं मद्गृहे सोऽथ लोभनायागमिष्यति ..
स च कृत्रिम वेषेण निषेद्धव्यस्त्वया हि सः ..
स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय द्वारदेशं समाश्रितः .. 6 ..
5.157.m: "Now he will come to my house to entice [you]. / He is in a disguise, and you must surely turn him away." / Having agreed with "So be it," [the eunuch] took his post at the doorway. (6)

5.157.s:
puṣpo'pi cābravīdbhāryāṃ māhikākhyāṃ tataḥ param ..
māhikedya mayā dṛṣṭaḥ svatātaḥ svapuraḥ sthitaḥ .. 7 ..
5.157.d:
पुष्पोऽपि चाब्रवीद्भार्यां माहिकाख्यां ततः परम् ..
माहिकेद्य मया दृष्टः स्वतातः स्वपुरः स्थितः .. 7 ..
5.157.m: Then Puṣpa spoke to the wife named Māhikā: / "Māhikā, today I saw your father standing before me, (7)

5.157.s:
vīrabhadraḥ suduḥkhārto malināṃbarasaṃvṛtaḥ ..
abravīcca tataḥ kopānmāmevaṃ paruṣākṣaram .. 8 ..
5.157.d:
वीरभद्रः सुदुःखार्तो मलिनांबरसंवृतः ..
अब्रवीच्च ततः कोपान्मामेवं परुषाक्षरम् .. 8 ..
5.157.m: Vīrabhadra, sorely afflicted with grief, clad in dirty clothes. / Then in anger he spoke to me these harsh words: (8)

5.157.s:
dhigdhikpāpa tvayā kanyātīva rūpavatī sadā ..
vaṃcayitvā janetāramudūḍhā sā sumadhyamā .. 9 ..
5.157.d:
धिग्धिक्पाप त्वया कन्यातीव रूपवती सदा ..
वंचयित्वा जनेतारमुदूढा सा सुमध्यमा .. 9 ..
5.157.m: 'Fie, fie on you, sinner! A girl always exceedingly beautiful, / having deceived her father, that slender-waisted one was married by you. (9)

5.157.s:
na dattaṃ tatpituḥ kiṃcinna tasyā atha putraka ..
vidhavāṃ yādṛśīṃ tāṃ ca śvetāṃbaradharāṃ sadā .. 6.158.10 ..
5.157.d:
न दत्तं तत्पितुः किंचिन्न तस्या अथ पुत्रक ..
विधवां यादृशीं तां च श्वेतांबरधरां सदा .. 6.158.10 ..
5.157.m: Nothing was given to her father, nor to her, O son. / And you keep her like a widow, always wearing white garments, (10)

5.157.s:
saṃdhārayasi pāpātmanneṣṭaṃ bhojyaṃ prayacchasi ..
tasmāttasyāḥ piturdehi tvaṃ suvarṇāyutaṃ dhruvam .. 11 ..
5.157.d:
संधारयसि पापात्मन्नेष्टं भोज्यं प्रयच्छसि ..
तस्मात्तस्याः पितुर्देहि त्वं सुवर्णायुतं ध्रुवम् .. 11 ..
5.157.m: O sinful soul, and do not provide desirable food. / Therefore, surely give ten thousand gold coins to her father, (11)

5.157.s:
bhūṣaṇaṃ vāṃchitaṃ tasyā yattadvai rucipūrvakam ..
yena saṃdhārayedbhāryā sā''naṃdaṃ paramaṃ gatā .. 12 ..
5.157.d:
भूषणं वांछितं तस्या यत्तद्वै रुचिपूर्वकम् ..
येन संधारयेद्भार्या सा'ऽनंदं परमं गता .. 12 ..
5.157.m: and whatever ornament is desired by her according to her taste, / so that your wife, having attained supreme joy, may put it on. (12)

5.157.s:
nirānaṃdā yato nārī na garbhaṃ dhārayetsphuṭam ..
niḥsaṃtāno yato vaṃśaḥ svargādapi kṣitiṃ vrajet .. 13 ..
5.157.d:
निरानंदा यतो नारी न गर्भं धारयेत्स्फुटम् ..
निःसंतानो यतो वंशः स्वर्गादपि क्षितिं व्रजेत् .. 13 ..
5.157.m: For a woman devoid of joy clearly does not bear a womb; / and a family without offspring falls even from heaven to the earth. (13)

5.157.s:
sa patiṣyatyasaṃdigdhaṃ kulāṃgāreṇa ca tvayā ..
sā tvamānaya vastrāṇi gṛhamadhyācchubhāni ca .. 14 ..
5.157.d:
स पतिष्यत्यसंदिग्धं कुलांगारेण च त्वया ..
सा त्वमानय वस्त्राणि गृहमध्याच्छुभानि च .. 14 ..
5.157.m: Through you, a disgrace to your family, it will fall without doubt.' / Therefore, bring fine clothes from inside the house, (14)

5.157.s:
yāni dattāni bhūpena vyavahāraistadā mama ..
pañcāṃgaśca prasādo yo mayā prāptaśca taiḥ saha .. 15 ..
5.157.d:
यानि दत्तानि भूपेन व्यवहारैस्तदा मम ..
पञ्चांगश्च प्रसादो यो मया प्राप्तश्च तैः सह .. 15 ..
5.157.m: which were given to me then by the king on account of [legal] proceedings, / along with the fivefold royal gift that was received by me. (15)

5.157.s:
tvaṃ saṃdhāraya gātraiḥ svaiḥ śīghraṃ rasavatīṃ kuru ..
bhojanāyaiva śīghraṃ tu tvayā sārdhaṃ karomyaham .. 16 ..
5.157.d:
त्वं संधारय गात्रैः स्वैः शीघ्रं रसवतीं कुरु ..
भोजनायैव शीघ्रं तु त्वया सार्धं करोम्यहम् .. 16 ..
5.157.m: Put them upon your limbs, and quickly prepare tasty food; / I shall eat quickly with you, (16)

5.157.s:
ekasminnapi pātre ca tadādeśādasaṃśayam ..
sāpi sarvaṃ tathā cakre yaduktaṃ tena harṣitā .. 17 ..
5.157.d:
एकस्मिन्नपि पात्रे च तदादेशादसंशयम् ..
सापि सर्वं तथा चक्रे यदुक्तं तेन हर्षिता .. 17 ..
5.157.m: even from a single plate, without a doubt, according to his instruction." / She too, delighted, did everything just as he had spoken, (17)

5.157.s:
bhojanācchādanaṃ caiva nirvikalpena cetasā ..
tataḥ kāmāturaḥ puṣpo maithunāyopacakrame .. 18 ..
5.157.d:
भोजनाच्छादनं चैव निर्विकल्पेन चेतसा ..
ततः कामातुरः पुष्पो मैथुनायोपचक्रमे .. 18 ..
5.157.m: providing food and clothing with an unquestioning mind. / Then Puṣpa, afflicted with desire, approached for sexual union. (18)

5.157.s:
etasminnaṃtare prāpto maṇibhadraḥ samutsukaḥ ..
kṣutkṣāmaḥ sa pipāsārto vyavahārotthalipsayā .. 19 ..
5.157.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राप्तो मणिभद्रः समुत्सुकः ..
क्षुत्क्षामः स पिपासार्तो व्यवहारोत्थलिप्सया .. 19 ..
5.157.m: In the meantime, Maṇibhadra arrived, eager, / emaciated with hunger, tormented by thirst, eager for gain arising from business. (19)

5.157.s:
praveśaṃ kurute yāvadgṛhamadhye samutsukaḥ ..
niṣiddhastena ṣaṇḍhena bhartsayitvā muhurmuhuḥ .. 6.158.20 ..
5.157.d:
प्रवेशं कुरुते यावद्गृहमध्ये समुत्सुकः ..
निषिद्धस्तेन षण्ढेन भर्त्सयित्वा मुहुर्मुहुः .. 6.158.20 ..
5.157.m: As he eagerly entered the house, / he was turned away by that eunuch, being scolded again and again. (20)

5.157.s:
haṭhādyāvatpraveśaṃ sa cakāra nijamaṃdire ..
tāvacca daṇḍakāṣṭhena mastake tena tāḍitaḥ .. 21 ..
5.157.d:
हठाद्यावत्प्रवेशं स चकार निजमंदिरे ..
तावच्च दण्डकाष्ठेन मस्तके तेन ताडितः .. 21 ..
5.157.m: As soon as he forcefully entered his own dwelling, / he was struck on the head by him with a wooden club. (21)

5.157.s:
atha saṃpatito bhūmau mūrchayā saṃpariplutaḥ ..
kartavyaṃ naiva jānāti tatprahāraprapīḍitaḥ .. 22 ..
5.157.d:
अथ संपतितो भूमौ मूर्छया संपरिप्लुतः ..
कर्तव्यं नैव जानाति तत्प्रहारप्रपीडितः .. 22 ..
5.157.m: Then he collapsed to the ground, overcome by fainting; / afflicted by that blow, he did not know what to do at all. (22)

5.157.s:
tataḥ kolāhalo jātastasya dvāre gṛhasya ca ..
janasya saṃprayātasya hāhākāraparasya ca .. 23 ..
5.157.d:
ततः कोलाहलो जातस्तस्य द्वारे गृहस्य च ..
जनस्य संप्रयातस्य हाहाकारपरस्य च .. 23 ..
5.157.m: Then an uproar arose at the door of his house, / with people gathering and crying out in dismay. (23)

5.157.s:
papracchustaṃ janāḥ keci ddhikpāpa kimidaṃ kṛtam ..
vṛttibhaṃgaḥ kṛto'nena atha tvaṃ vyaṃtarārditaḥ .. 24 ..
5.157.d:
पप्रच्छुस्तं जनाः केचि द्धिक्पाप किमिदं कृतम् ..
वृत्तिभंगः कृतोऽनेन अथ त्वं व्यंतरार्दितः .. 24 ..
5.157.m: Some people asked him: "Fie, sinner! What is this that was done? / Was your livelihood destroyed by him, or are you possessed by an evil spirit, (24)

5.157.s: imāmavasthāṃ yannītaḥ saṃprāpto'si nṛpādvadham .. 25 ..
5.157.d: इमामवस्थां यन्नीतः संप्राप्तोऽसि नृपाद्वधम् .. 25 ..
5.157.m: that you have brought him to this state? You have earned death from the king!" (25)

5.157.s:
.. ṣaṃḍha uvāca .. ..
na vṛttirgarhitā tena nāhaṃ vyaṃtarapīḍitaḥ ..
maṇibhadro na caiṣa syādeṣa veṣakaraḥ pumān .. 26 ..
5.157.d:
.. षंढ उवाच .. ..
न वृत्तिर्गर्हिता तेन नाहं व्यंतरपीडितः ..
मणिभद्रो न चैष स्यादेष वेषकरः पुमान् .. 26 ..
5.157.m: The eunuch said: / "My livelihood was not ruined by him, nor am I afflicted by an evil spirit. / Nor is this man Maṇibhadra; this is an impostor. (26)

5.157.s:
māṇibhadraṃ vapuḥ kṛtvā saṃprāpto yācituṃ dhanam ..
haṭhātpraviśyamānastu sa mayā mūrdhni tāḍitaḥ .. 27 ..
5.157.d:
माणिभद्रं वपुः कृत्वा संप्राप्तो याचितुं धनम् ..
हठात्प्रविश्यमानस्तु स मया मूर्ध्नि ताडितः .. 27 ..
5.157.m: Having assumed Maṇibhadra's form, he arrived to beg for money. / Entering by force, he was struck on the head by me. (27)

5.157.s:
maṇibhadro gṛhasyāṃtarbhuktvā śayanamāśritaḥ ..
saṃtiṣṭhate na jānāti vṛttāṃtamidamā sthitam .. 28 ..
5.157.d:
मणिभद्रो गृहस्यांतर्भुक्त्वा शयनमाश्रितः ..
संतिष्ठते न जानाति वृत्तांतमिदमा स्थितम् .. 28 ..
5.157.m: Maṇibhadra, having eaten, is resting upon his bed inside the house; / he stays there and does not know this situation that has occurred." (28)

5.157.s:
tataḥ puṣpo'pi tacchrutvā taṃ ca kolāhalaṃ bahiḥ ..
maṇibhadrasya rūpeṇa dvāradeśaṃ samāgataḥ .. 29 ..
5.157.d:
ततः पुष्पोऽपि तच्छ्रुत्वा तं च कोलाहलं बहिः ..
मणिभद्रस्य रूपेण द्वारदेशं समागतः .. 29 ..
5.157.m: Then Puṣpa too, hearing that uproar outside, / came to the doorway in the form of Maṇibhadra. (29)

5.157.s:
abravīnnityamabhyeti mama rūpeṇa cādhamaḥ ..
eṣa veṣadharaḥ kaścidyācituṃ dhanameva hi .. 6.158.30 ..
5.157.d:
अब्रवीन्नित्यमभ्येति मम रूपेण चाधमः ..
एष वेषधरः कश्चिद्याचितुं धनमेव हि .. 6.158.30 ..
5.157.m: He said: "This vile person constantly comes in my form; / he is some impostor, [coming] merely to beg for money. (30)

5.157.s:
etenāpi ca ṣaṃḍhena na ca bhadramanuṣṭhitam ..
yatkubjo'yaṃ hato mūrdhni yācituṃ samu pasthitaḥ .. 31 ..
5.157.d:
एतेनापि च षंढेन न च भद्रमनुष्ठितम् ..
यत्कुब्जोऽयं हतो मूर्ध्नि याचितुं समु पस्थितः .. 31 ..
5.157.m: Even so, this eunuch did not act properly, / in that this hunchback, having approached to beg, was struck on the head." (31)

5.157.s:
etasminnantare so'pi cetanāṃ prāpya kṛtsnaśaḥ ..
vīkṣate purato yāvattāvadātmasamaḥ pumān .. 32 ..
5.157.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे सोऽपि चेतनां प्राप्य कृत्स्नशः ..
वीक्षते पुरतो यावत्तावदात्मसमः पुमान् .. 32 ..
5.157.m: In the meantime, having fully regained consciousness, / he looked in front of him and saw a man just like himself. (32)

5.157.s: sarvataḥ sa tamālokya tato vacanamabravīt .. 33 ..
5.157.d: सर्वतः स तमालोक्य ततो वचनमब्रवीत् .. 33 ..
5.157.m: Looking at him on all sides, he then spoke these words: (33)

5.157.s:
kva coraḥ saṃpraviṣṭo me mama rūpeṇa maṃdire ..
bhedayitvā tu ṣaṇḍākhyamevaṃ dattvā ca vāsasī .. 34 ..
5.157.d:
क्व चोरः संप्रविष्टो मे मम रूपेण मंदिरे ..
भेदयित्वा तु षण्डाख्यमेवं दत्त्वा च वाससी .. 34 ..
5.157.m: "Where has this thief, entered into my house in my form, / having corrupted the eunuch and given him two garments? (34)

5.157.s:
yāvadbhūpagṛhaṃ gatvā tvāṃ ṣaṃḍhena samanvitam ..
vadhāya yojayāmyeva tāvaddrutataraṃ vraja .. 35 ..
5.157.d:
यावद्भूपगृहं गत्वा त्वां षंढेन समन्वितम् ..
वधाय योजयाम्येव तावद्द्रुततरं व्रज .. 35 ..
5.157.m: Go away very quickly, before I go to the king's palace / and have you executed along with the eunuch!" (35)

5.157.s:
.. puṣpa uvāca .. ..
mama rūpaṃ samādhāya tvamāyāto gṛhe mama ..
śūnyaṃ matvā tato jñātastvayā'haṃ gṛhasaṃsthitaḥ ..36..
5.157.d:
.. पुष्प उवाच .. ..
मम रूपं समाधाय त्वमायातो गृहे मम ..
शून्यं मत्वा ततो ज्ञातस्त्वयाऽहं गृहसंस्थितः ..36..
5.157.m: Puṣpa said: / "Having assumed my form, you came to my house, / thinking it empty; then you discovered me staying in the house. (36)

5.157.s:
tato nṛpāya dāsyāmi vadhārthaṃ ca na saṃśayaḥ ..
no cedgaccha drutaṃ pāpa yadi jīvitumicchasi ..37.. ..
5.157.d:
ततो नृपाय दास्यामि वधार्थं च न संशयः ..
नो चेद्गच्छ द्रुतं पाप यदि जीवितुमिच्छसि ..37.. ..
5.157.m: Therefore I will hand [you] over to the king for execution, without a doubt. / Otherwise, go quickly, sinner, if you wish to live!" (37)

5.157.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evamukttvā tatastau ca bāhuyuddhena vai mithaḥ ..
yudhyamānau narairanyaiḥ kṛcchreṇa tu nivāritau ..38..
5.157.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्त्त्वा ततस्तौ च बाहुयुद्धेन वै मिथः ..
युध्यमानौ नरैरन्यैः कृच्छ्रेण तु निवारितौ ..38..
5.157.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, the two of them, fighting with each other in hand-to-hand combat, / were restrained with difficulty by other men. (38)

5.157.s:
tataste svajanā ye tu maṇibha drasya cāgatāḥ ..
parijānaṃti no dvābhyāṃ viśeṣaṃ māṇibhadrakam .. 39 ..
5.157.d:
ततस्ते स्वजना ये तु मणिभ द्रस्य चागताः ..
परिजानंति नो द्वाभ्यां विशेषं माणिभद्रकम् .. 39 ..
5.157.m: Then those kinsmen of Maṇibhadra who had arrived / could not discern any difference between the two as to which was Maṇibhadra. (39)

5.157.s:
vālisugrīvayoryuddhaṃ tārārthe yudhyamānayoḥ ..
evaṃ vivadamānau tu krodhatāmrā yatekṣaṇau .. 6.158.40 ..
5.157.d:
वालिसुग्रीवयोर्युद्धं तारार्थे युध्यमानयोः ..
एवं विवदमानौ तु क्रोधताम्रा यतेक्षणौ .. 6.158.40 ..
5.157.m: [It was like] the battle between Vālin and Sugrīva fighting for the sake of Tārā. / Thus disputing, their eyes red and wide with anger, (40)

5.157.s:
rājadvāraṃ samāsādya sthitau svajanasaṃvṛtau ..
dvāḥsthena sūcitau rājñe sabhātalamupasthitau .. 41 ..
5.157.d:
राजद्वारं समासाद्य स्थितौ स्वजनसंवृतौ ..
द्वाःस्थेन सूचितौ राज्ञे सभातलमुपस्थितौ .. 41 ..
5.157.m: they stood, surrounded by their kinsmen, having reached the royal gate. / Announced to the king by the door-keeper, they arrived at the assembly hall. (41)

5.157.s:
cauracaureti jalpantau para sparavadhaiṣiṇau ..
bhūbhujā vīkṣitau tau ca dvijau tu dvijasattamāḥ ..42 ..
5.157.d:
चौरचौरेति जल्पन्तौ पर स्परवधैषिणौ ..
भूभुजा वीक्षितौ तौ च द्विजौ तु द्विजसत्तमाः ..42 ..
5.157.m: Shouting 'Thief! Thief!' and desiring each other's death, / those two brahmins were looked upon by the king, O best of brahmins. (42)

5.157.s:
na viśeṣo'sti viśleṣastayorekopikāyataḥ ..
tataśca vyavahāreṣu samatī teṣu vai tadā .. 43 ..
5.157.d:
न विशेषोऽस्ति विश्लेषस्तयोरेकोपिकायतः ..
ततश्च व्यवहारेषु समती तेषु वै तदा .. 43 ..
5.157.m: There was no difference or distinction in the body of either one of them. / Then, with regard to past transactions, (43)

5.157.s:
pṛṣṭau guhyeṣu sarveṣu pratyakṣeṣu viśeṣataḥ..
vadatastau yathāvṛttaṃ pṛthakpṛthagvyavasthitam .. 44 ..
5.157.d:
पृष्टौ गुह्येषु सर्वेषु प्रत्यक्षेषु विशेषतः..
वदतस्तौ यथावृत्तं पृथक्पृथग्व्यवस्थितम् .. 44 ..
5.157.m: they were questioned about all private matters and especially about public ones; / both of them recounted what had happened, separately and accurately. (44)

5.157.s:
tatastu svajanaiḥ sarvaireko nītva tha cānyataḥ ..
pṛṣṭo gotrānvayaṃ sarvaṃ dvitīyastu tataḥ param .. 45 ..
5.157.d:
ततस्तु स्वजनैः सर्वैरेको नीत्व थ चान्यतः ..
पृष्टो गोत्रान्वयं सर्वं द्वितीयस्तु ततः परम् .. 45 ..
5.157.m: Then, one of them was taken aside by all the kinsmen / and questioned about his entire lineage and family, and the second one after that. (45)

5.157.s:
teṣāmapi tathā sarvaṃ yathāsamyaṅniveditam ..
atha rājā bṛhatsenaḥ sarvāṃstāni damabravīt .. 46 ..
5.157.d:
तेषामपि तथा सर्वं यथासम्यङ्निवेदितम् ..
अथ राजा बृहत्सेनः सर्वांस्तानि दमब्रवीत् .. 46 ..
5.157.m: Everything was correctly explained by them in the exact same manner. / Then King Bṛhatsena spoke this to all of them: (46)

5.157.s:
patnī cānīyatāṃ tasya maṇibhadrasya vai gṛhāt ..
nijakāntasya vijñāne sā pramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 47 ..
5.157.d:
पत्नी चानीयतां तस्य मणिभद्रस्य वै गृहात् ..
निजकान्तस्य विज्ञाने सा प्रमाणं भविष्यति .. 47 ..
5.157.m: "Let that wife of Maṇibhadra be brought from the house; / she will be the authoritative witness in recognising her own husband." (47)

5.157.s:
tato gatvā ca sā proktā puruṣairnṛpasaṃbhavaiḥ ..
āgaccha kāṃtaṃ jānīhi tvaṃ pramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyasi .. 48 ..
5.157.d:
ततो गत्वा च सा प्रोक्ता पुरुषैर्नृपसंभवैः ..
आगच्छ कांतं जानीहि त्वं प्रमाणं भविष्यसि .. 48 ..
5.157.m: Then royal messengers, having gone, said to her: / "Come, identify your husband; you shall be the authoritative witness." (44)

5.157.s:
tataḥ sā vrīḍayā yuktā pracchāditaśirāstataḥ ..
nṛpāgre saṃsthitā proce viddhisamyaṅnijaṃ priyam .. 49 ..
5.157.d:
ततः सा व्रीडया युक्ता प्रच्छादितशिरास्ततः ..
नृपाग्रे संस्थिता प्रोचे विद्धिसम्यङ्निजं प्रियम् .. 49 ..
5.157.m: Then she, filled with bashfulness, with her head veiled, / stood before the king and was addressed: "Accurately recognise your own beloved!" (49)

5.157.s: na vayaṃ niścayaṃ vidmo na caite svajanāstava .. 6.158.50 ..
5.157.d: न वयं निश्चयं विद्मो न चैते स्वजनास्तव .. 6.158.50 ..
5.157.m: "We do not know with certainty, nor do these relatives of yours."

5.157.s:
tataḥ sā cintayāmāsa nijacitte varāṃganā ..
maṇibhadreṇa dagdhāhamīrṣyāvahnigatā'niśam .. 51 ..
5.157.d:
ततः सा चिन्तयामास निजचित्ते वरांगना ..
मणिभद्रेण दग्धाहमीर्ष्यावह्निगताऽनिशम् .. 51 ..
5.157.m:
Then that excellent woman thought in her own mind:
"I was burned by Maṇibhadra, constantly plunged into the fire of jealousy.

5.157.s:
vaṃcayitvā tu pitaraṃ gṛhītāsmi tataḥ param ..
na kiṃcitpāpmanā dattaṃ jalpayitvā dhanaṃ bahu .. .. 52 ..
5.157.d:
वंचयित्वा तु पितरं गृहीतास्मि ततः परम् ..
न किंचित्पाप्मना दत्तं जल्पयित्वा धनं बहु .. .. 52 ..
5.157.m:
Having deceived my father, I was taken afterwards;
and nothing was given by that sinner, after he had promised much wealth.

5.157.s:
dvitīyena tu me puṃsā martyaloke sukhaṃ kṛtam ..
dattvā vastrāṇi citrāṇi tathaivābharaṇāni ca .. 53 ..
5.157.d:
द्वितीयेन तु मे पुंसा मर्त्यलोके सुखं कृतम् ..
दत्त्वा वस्त्राणि चित्राणि तथैवाभरणानि च .. 53 ..
5.157.m:
By this second man, however, happiness was brought to me in the mortal world,
having given varied garments and likewise ornaments.

5.157.s:
pradāsyati ca tātasya suvarṇaṃ kathitaṃ ca yat ..
yadgṛhṇāmi svahastena maṇibhadraṃ dvitīyakam .. 54 ..
5.157.d:
प्रदास्यति च तातस्य सुवर्णं कथितं च यत् ..
यद्गृह्णामि स्वहस्तेन मणिभद्रं द्वितीयकम् .. 54 ..
5.157.m:
And he will give to my father the gold that was agreed,
if I take the second Maṇibhadra with my own hand."

5.157.s:
evaṃ niścitya manasā dṛṣṭvā raktapariplutam ..
prathamaṃ maṇibhadraṃ sā jagṛhe'tha dvitīyakam.. 55 ..
5.157.d:
एवं निश्चित्य मनसा दृष्ट्वा रक्तपरिप्लुतम् ..
प्रथमं मणिभद्रं सा जगृहेऽथ द्वितीयकम्.. 55 ..
5.157.m:
Having thus decided in her mind, seeing him drenched with blood,
she first [rejected] Maṇibhadra and then took the second.

5.157.s:
abravīcca tato vākyaṃ sarvalokasya śṛṇvataḥ ..
ahaṃ tātena dattāsya vivāhe agnisaṃnidhau ..56..
5.157.d:
अब्रवीच्च ततो वाक्यं सर्वलोकस्य शृण्वतः ..
अहं तातेन दत्तास्य विवाहे अग्निसंनिधौ ..56..
5.157.m:
And she then spoke words while all the people listened:
"I was given to this man by my father in marriage in the presence of the fire.

5.157.s:
dvitīyo'yaṃ durācāro veṣakartā samā gataḥ ..
māṃ ca prārthayate guptāṃ nānācāraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ .. 57 ..
5.157.d:
द्वितीयोऽयं दुराचारो वेषकर्ता समा गतः ..
मां च प्रार्थयते गुप्तां नानाचारैः पृथग्विधैः .. 57 ..
5.157.m:
This second man, a villain, an impostor in disguise, has arrived,
and he solicits me in secret by various distinct means."

5.157.s:
tatastu pārthivaḥ kruddhastasya śākhāvalaṃbanam ..
ādideśa dvijaśreṣṭhā maṇibhadrasya durmateḥ .. 58 ..
5.157.d:
ततस्तु पार्थिवः क्रुद्धस्तस्य शाखावलंबनम् ..
आदिदेश द्विजश्रेष्ठा मणिभद्रस्य दुर्मतेः .. 58 ..
5.157.m:
Then the king, enraged, ordered hanging from a branch
for that wicked-minded Maṇibhadra, O best of brahmins.

5.157.s:
etasminnaṃtare so'tha vadhakānāṃ samarpitaḥ ..
taṃ vṛkṣaṃ nīyamānastu ślokānetāṃstadāpaṭhat .. 59 ..
5.157.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे सोऽथ वधकानां समर्पितः ..
तं वृक्षं नीयमानस्तु श्लोकानेतांस्तदापठत् .. 59 ..
5.157.m:
In the meantime, he was handed over to the executioners;
and being led to that tree, he then recited these verses:

5.157.s:
nirdayatvaṃ tathā drohaṃ kuṭilatvaṃ viśeṣataḥ ..
aśaucaṃ nirghṛṇatvaṃ ca strīṇāṃ doṣāḥ svabhāvajāḥ .. 6.158.60 ..
5.157.d:
निर्दयत्वं तथा द्रोहं कुटिलत्वं विशेषतः ..
अशौचं निर्घृणत्वं च स्त्रीणां दोषाः स्वभावजाः .. 6.158.60 ..
5.157.m:
"Cruelty, betrayal, especially deceitfulness,
impurity, and pitilessness are the innate flaws of women.

5.157.s:
antarviṣamayā hyetā bahirbhāge manoramāḥ ..
guñjāphalasamākārā yoṣitaḥ sarva daivahi .. 61 ..
5.157.d:
अन्तर्विषमया ह्येता बहिर्भागे मनोरमाः ..
गुञ्जाफलसमाकारा योषितः सर्व दैवहि .. 61 ..
5.157.m:
For inside they are full of poison, while attractive on the outside,
women are always indeed like the seeds of the guñjā berry.

5.157.s:
uśanā veda yacchāstraṃ yacca veda bṛhaspatiḥ ..
manvādayastathānye'pi strībuddhestatra kiṃca na .. 62 ..
5.157.d:
उशना वेद यच्छास्त्रं यच्च वेद बृहस्पतिः ..
मन्वादयस्तथान्येऽपि स्त्रीबुद्धेस्तत्र किंच न .. 62 ..
5.157.m:
The treatise that Uśanas knows, and that which Bṛhaspati knows,
and Manu and the others too—in comparison to the cunning of women, that is nothing.

5.157.s:
pīyūṣamadhare vāsaṃ hṛdi hālāhalaṃ viṣam ..
āsvādyate'dharastena hṛdayaṃ ca prapīḍyate .. 63 ..
5.157.d:
पीयूषमधरे वासं हृदि हालाहलं विषम् ..
आस्वाद्यतेऽधरस्तेन हृदयं च प्रपीड्यते .. 63 ..
5.157.m:
Nectar dwells on the lower lip, [but] deadly hālāhala poison is in the heart;
therefore the lip is savored, and the heart is tormented.

5.157.s:
alaktako yathā rakto naraḥ kāmī tathaiva ca ..
hṛtasārastathā so'pi pādamūle nipā tyate .. 64 ..
5.157.d:
अलक्तको यथा रक्तो नरः कामी तथैव च ..
हृतसारस्तथा सोऽपि पादमूले निपा त्यते .. 64 ..
5.157.m:
Just as alaktaka dye is red, so is an impassioned man;
and drained of its essence, he too is cast down at the soles of her feet.

5.157.s:
saṃsāraviṣavṛkṣasya kukarmakusumasya ca ..
narakārtiphalasyoktā mūlameṣā nitaṃbinī .. 65 ..
5.157.d:
संसारविषवृक्षस्य कुकर्मकुसुमस्य च ..
नरकार्तिफलस्योक्ता मूलमेषा नितंबिनी .. 65 ..
5.157.m:
Of the poison-tree of worldly existence, whose flower is evil deeds,
and whose fruit is the agony of hell, a slender woman is called the root.

5.157.s: kasya no jāyate trāso dṛṣṭvā dūrā dapi striyam.. 66 ..
5.157.d: कस्य नो जायते त्रासो दृष्ट्वा दूरा दपि स्त्रियम्.. 66 ..
5.157.m: In whom does terror not arise upon seeing a woman even from afar?

5.157.s:
saṃsārabhramaṇaṃ nārī prathame'pi samāgame ..
vahnipradakṣiṇanyāyavyājenaiva pradarśayet .. 67 ..
5.157.d:
संसारभ्रमणं नारी प्रथमेऽपि समागमे ..
वह्निप्रदक्षिणन्यायव्याजेनैव प्रदर्शयेत् .. 67 ..
5.157.m:
A woman would show the wandering of worldly existence even at the first encounter,
under the mere pretext of circumambulating the fire.

5.157.s:
etāstu nirghṛṇatvena nirdaya tvena nityaśaḥ ..
viśeṣājjāḍyakṛtyena dūṣayaṃti kulatrayam .. 68 ..
5.157.d:
एतास्तु निर्घृणत्वेन निर्दय त्वेन नित्यशः ..
विशेषाज्जाड्यकृत्येन दूषयंति कुलत्रयम् .. 68 ..
5.157.m:
These women, through ruthless and pitiless behavior at all times,
especially by their foolish acts, bring ruin upon the three lineages.

5.157.s:
kulatrayagṛhaṃ kīrtyā nijayā dhavalīkṛtam ..
kṛṣṇaṃ karotyakṛ tyena nārī dīpaśikheva tu .. 69 ..
5.157.d:
कुलत्रयगृहं कीर्त्या निजया धवलीकृतम् ..
कृष्णं करोत्यकृ त्येन नारी दीपशिखेव तु .. 69 ..
5.157.m:
A woman, like the flame of a lamp, blackens by improper conduct
the mansion of the three lineages that has been made white by its own fame.

5.157.s:
dharmavṛkṣasya vātālī cittapadmaśaśiprabhā ..
sṛṣṭā kāmārṇavagrāhī kena mokṣadṛḍhārgalā .. 6.158.70 ..
5.157.d:
धर्मवृक्षस्य वाताली चित्तपद्मशशिप्रभा ..
सृष्टा कामार्णवग्राही केन मोक्षदृढार्गला .. 6.158.70 ..
5.157.m:
A whirlwind to the tree of dharma, the moon's radiance to the lotus of the mind,
a female crocodile in the ocean of desire, a stout bolt across [the door to] liberation—by whom was woman created?

5.157.s:
kārā saṃtānakūṭasya saṃsāravanavāgurā ..
svargamārgamahāgartā puṃsāṃ strī vedhasā kṛtā .. 71 ..
5.157.d:
कारा संतानकूटस्य संसारवनवागुरा ..
स्वर्गमार्गमहागर्ता पुंसां स्त्री वेधसा कृता .. 71 ..
5.157.m:
A prison for the snare of lineage, a net in the forest of saṃsāra,
a great pit on the path to heaven—woman was made for men by the Creator.

5.157.s:
vedhasā baṃdhanaṃ kiṃcinnṛṇāmanyadapaśyatā ..
strīrūpeṇa tataḥ ko'pi pāśo'yaṃ sudṛḍhaḥ kṛtaḥ ..72..
5.157.d:
वेधसा बंधनं किंचिन्नृणामन्यदपश्यता ..
स्त्रीरूपेण ततः कोऽपि पाशोऽयं सुदृढः कृतः ..72..
5.157.m:
Seeing no other bondage for men, the Creator
then made this extremely strong snare in the form of woman."

5.157.s:
ityevaṃ bahudhā so'pi vilalāpa suduḥkhitaḥ ..
strīcintāṃ bahudhā kṛtvā ātmānaṃ cāpyagarhayat .. 73 ..
5.157.d:
इत्येवं बहुधा सोऽपि विललाप सुदुःखितः ..
स्त्रीचिन्तां बहुधा कृत्वा आत्मानं चाप्यगर्हयत् .. 73 ..
5.157.m:
Thus in various ways he lamented, deeply sorrowful;
reflecting on women at length, he also reproached himself:

5.157.s:
aho kubuddhinā naiva labdhaṃ saṃsārajaṃ phalam..
na kadācinmayā dattaṃ tṛṣṇāvyākulacetasā .. 74 ..
5.157.d:
अहो कुबुद्धिना नैव लब्धं संसारजं फलम्..
न कदाचिन्मया दत्तं तृष्णाव्याकुलचेतसा .. 74 ..
5.157.m:
"Alas! Being foolish, the fruit born of worldly life was not obtained by me at all;
with a mind agitated by greed, nothing was ever given by me.

5.157.s:
aiśvarye'pi sthite bhūri na mayā sukṛtaṃ kṛtam ..
kadācinnaiva japtaṃ ca na hutaṃ ca hutāśane .. 75 ..
5.157.d:
ऐश्वर्येऽपि स्थिते भूरि न मया सुकृतं कृतम् ..
कदाचिन्नैव जप्तं च न हुतं च हुताशने .. 75 ..
5.157.m:
Even while great wealth was present, no virtuous deed was done by me;
never was a mantra recited, nor was an oblation offered into the fire.

5.157.s:
athavā satyamevoktaṃ kenāpi ca mahātmanā ..
kṛpaṇena samo dātā na bhūto na bhaviṣyati ..
aspṛṣṭvāpi ca vittaṃ svaṃ yaḥ parebhyaḥ prayacchati .. 76 ..
5.157.d:
अथवा सत्यमेवोक्तं केनापि च महात्मना ..
कृपणेन समो दाता न भूतो न भविष्यति ..
अस्पृष्ट्वापि च वित्तं स्वं यः परेभ्यः प्रयच्छति .. 76 ..
5.157.m:
Or rather, it was truly said by some great-souled person:
There has never been nor will there ever be a giver equal to a miser,
who, without even touching his wealth, gives it away to others.

5.157.s:
śaraṇaṃ kiṃ prapannānāṃ viṣavanmārayaṃti kim ..
na dīyate na bhujyaṃte kṛpaṇena dhanāni ca .. 77 ..
5.157.d:
शरणं किं प्रपन्नानां विषवन्मारयंति किम् ..
न दीयते न भुज्यंते कृपणेन धनानि च .. 77 ..
5.157.m:
What refuge is there for those who surrender? Do they kill like poison?
Riches are neither given away nor enjoyed by a miser.

5.157.s:
dānaṃ bhogo nāśastisro gatayo bhavaṃti vittasya ..
yo na dadāti na bhuṃkte tasya tṛtīyā gatirbhavati .. 78 ..
5.157.d:
दानं भोगो नाशस्तिस्रो गतयो भवंति वित्तस्य ..
यो न ददाति न भुंक्ते तस्य तृतीया गतिर्भवति .. 78 ..
5.157.m:
Giving, enjoyment, and loss are the three destinies of wealth;
for him who neither gives nor enjoys, the third destiny occurs.

5.157.s:
dhaninopyadānavibhavā gaṇyaṃte dhuri daridrāṇām..
nahi haṃti yatpipāsāmataḥ samudro'pi marureva .. 79 ..
5.157.d:
धनिनोप्यदानविभवा गण्यंते धुरि दरिद्राणाम्..
नहि हंति यत्पिपासामतः समुद्रोऽपि मरुरेव .. 79 ..
5.157.m:
Rich men who have riches without giving are counted at the head of the destitute;
since it does not quench thirst, even the ocean is nothing but a desert.

5.157.s:
atyupayuktāḥ sadbhirgatāgatairaharahaḥ sunirviṇṇāḥ ..
kṛpaṇajanasaṃnikāśaṃ saṃprāpyārthāḥ svapaṃtīha .. 6.158.80 ..
5.157.d:
अत्युपयुक्ताः सद्भिर्गतागतैरहरहः सुनिर्विण्णाः ..
कृपणजनसंनिकाशं संप्राप्यार्थाः स्वपंतीह .. 6.158.80 ..
5.157.m:
Utterly worn out by good people who come and go day after day, completely exhausted,
wealth comes to the presence of misers and falls asleep here.

5.157.s:
prāptānna labhaṃte te bhogānbhoktuṃ svakarmaṇā kṛpaṇāḥ ..
mukhapākaḥ kila bhavati drākṣāpāke balibhujānām .. 81 ..
5.157.d:
प्राप्तान्न लभंते ते भोगान्भोक्तुं स्वकर्मणा कृपणाः ..
मुखपाकः किल भवति द्राक्षापाके बलिभुजानाम् .. 81 ..
5.157.m:
Misers do not get to enjoy the pleasures they have obtained, on account of their own deeds;
inflammation of the mouth indeed occurs for crows when the grapes are ripe.

5.157.s:
dātavyaṃ bhoktavyaṃ sati vibhave saṃcayo na kartavyaḥ ..
paśyeha madhukarīṇāṃ saṃcitamarthaṃ haraṃtyanye .. 82 ..
5.157.d:
दातव्यं भोक्तव्यं सति विभवे संचयो न कर्तव्यः ..
पश्येह मधुकरीणां संचितमर्थं हरंत्यन्ये .. 82 ..
5.157.m:
One should give, one should enjoy when wealth is present; hoarding should not be done;
look here, others carry off the wealth accumulated by female bees.

5.157.s:
yācitaṃ dvijavare na dīyate saṃcitaṃ kratuvare na yojyate ..
tatkadaryaparirakṣitaṃ dhanaṃ caurapārthivagṛheṣu bhujyate .. 83 ..
5.157.d:
याचितं द्विजवरे न दीयते संचितं क्रतुवरे न योज्यते ..
तत्कदर्यपरिरक्षितं धनं चौरपार्थिवगृहेषु भुज्यते .. 83 ..
5.157.m:
What is begged is not given to an excellent brahmin; what is gathered is not employed in a great sacrifice;
that wealth preserved by a skinflint is enjoyed in the houses of thieves and kings.

5.157.s:
tyāgo guṇo vittavatāṃ vittaṃ tyāgavatāṃ guṇaḥ ..
parasparaviyuktau tu vitta tyāgau viḍambanam .. 84 ..
5.157.d:
त्यागो गुणो वित्तवतां वित्तं त्यागवतां गुणः ..
परस्परवियुक्तौ तु वित्त त्यागौ विडम्बनम् .. 84 ..
5.157.m:
Giving is an ornament for the wealthy; wealth is an ornament for the generous;
but separated from one another, wealth and giving are a mockery.

5.157.s:
kiṃ tayā kriyate lakṣmyā yā vadhūriva kevalā ..
yā na veśyeva sāmānyā pathikairapi bhujyate .. 85 ..
5.157.d:
किं तया क्रियते लक्ष्म्या या वधूरिव केवला ..
या न वेश्येव सामान्या पथिकैरपि भुज्यते .. 85 ..
5.157.m:
What is to be done with that fortune which is merely like a bride,
and which is not enjoyed even by travelers, like a common courtesan?

5.157.s:
arthoṣmaṇā bhavetprāṇo bhavedbhakṣyairvinā nṛṇām ..
yataḥ saṃdhāryate bhūmiḥ kṛpaṇasyoṣmaṇā hi sā .. 86 ..
5.157.d:
अर्थोष्मणा भवेत्प्राणो भवेद्भक्ष्यैर्विना नृणाम् ..
यतः संधार्यते भूमिः कृपणस्योष्मणा हि सा .. 86 ..
5.157.m:
Human life might exist through the warmth of wealth without food,
since the earth itself is held up by the warmth of a miser.

5.157.s:
kṛpaṇānāṃ prasādena śeṣo dhārayate mahīm ..
yataste bhūgataṃ vittaṃ kurvate tasya coṣmaṇā .. 87 ..
5.157.d:
कृपणानां प्रसादेन शेषो धारयते महीम् ..
यतस्ते भूगतं वित्तं कुर्वते तस्य चोष्मणा .. 87 ..
5.157.m:
By the favor of misers Śeṣa holds the earth,
because they put their wealth into the ground, and by its warmth [he supports it]."

5.157.s:
evaṃ bahuvidhā vācaḥ pralapanmaṇibhadrakaḥ ..
nītvā taiḥ pārthivoddiṣṭaiḥ puruṣaiḥ paruṣākṣaram ..
bahudhā pralapaṃ ścaiva kṛtaḥ śākhāvalaṃbanaḥ .. 88 ..
5.157.d:
एवं बहुविधा वाचः प्रलपन्मणिभद्रकः ..
नीत्वा तैः पार्थिवोद्दिष्टैः पुरुषैः परुषाक्षरम् ..
बहुधा प्रलपं श्चैव कृतः शाखावलंबनः .. 88 ..
5.157.m:
While uttering words of many kinds in this manner, Maṇibhadra,
having been led by those men appointed by the king, speaking harsh words,
and while lamenting in many ways, was hanged from a tree branch.

5.157.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye maṇibhadropākhyāne maṇibhadranidhanavarṇanaṃnāmāṣṭapaṃcāśaduttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 158 ..
5.157.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये मणिभद्रोपाख्याने मणिभद्रनिधनवर्णनंनामाष्टपंचाशदुत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 158 ..
5.157.m: Thus ends the one hundred fifty-eighth chapter, named 'Description of the Death of Maṇibhadra', in the Maṇibhadra episode within the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection in the glorious Skandapurāṇa.

5.158.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
puṣpo'pi tāṃ samādāya māhikākhyāṃ varāṃganām ..
sa tadā prayayau hṛṣṭo maṇibhadrasya maṃdiram .. 1 ..
5.158.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
पुष्पोऽपि तां समादाय माहिकाख्यां वरांगनाम् ..
स तदा प्रययौ हृष्टो मणिभद्रस्य मंदिरम् .. 1 ..
5.158.m:
Sūta said:
Then Puṣpa too, having taken that excellent woman named Māhikā,
went gladly at that time to the palace of Maṇibhadra.

5.158.s:
śaṃkhatūryaninādena sarvaistaiḥ svajanairvṛtaḥ ..
na kasya tatra saṃbhūto vikalpastatsamudbhavaḥ .. 2 ..
5.158.d:
शंखतूर्यनिनादेन सर्वैस्तैः स्वजनैर्वृतः ..
न कस्य तत्र संभूतो विकल्पस्तत्समुद्भवः .. 2 ..
5.158.m:
Surrounded by all those relatives amidst the sound of conches and musical instruments,
no doubt arose in anyone there regarding him.

5.158.s:
bhāskarasya prasādena tathaivānyasya karhicit ..
so'pi maṃdiramāsādya yathātmapitṛsaṃbhavam .. 3 ..
5.158.d:
भास्करस्य प्रसादेन तथैवान्यस्य कर्हिचित् ..
सोऽपि मंदिरमासाद्य यथात्मपितृसंभवम् .. 3 ..
5.158.m: by the grace of the Sun, or sometimes by another's. / Having arrived at the house belonging to his own father,

5.158.s:
upaviśya tato madhye bandhūnsarvānsamāhvayat ..
adya tāvaddine mahyaṃ tulāgraṃ kamalā śritā .. 4 ..
5.158.d:
उपविश्य ततो मध्ये बन्धून्सर्वान्समाह्वयत् ..
अद्य तावद्दिने मह्यं तुलाग्रं कमला श्रिता .. 4 ..
5.158.m: and then sitting in the middle, he summoned all his kinsmen: / “Today, indeed, Lakṣmī has stood on the tip of my balance.

5.158.s:
calitāpi punaścāsyāḥ supatnyā vākyataḥ sthitā ..
kiyaṃtaṃ caiva kālaṃ me kārpaṇyaṃ mahadāsthitam .. 5 ..
5.158.d:
चलितापि पुनश्चास्याः सुपत्न्या वाक्यतः स्थिता ..
कियंतं चैव कालं मे कार्पण्यं महदास्थितम् .. 5 ..
5.158.m: Though she wavered, she stayed again through the words of this good wife. / For how long has great miserliness possessed me?

5.158.s:
jñātamadya calā lakṣmīstena tyaktaṃ sudūrataḥ ..
tasmādbaṃdhujanaiḥ sārdhaṃ devairvipraiśca kṛtsnaśaḥ ..
saṃvibhaktāṃ kariṣyāmi satyenātmānamālabhe .. 6 ..
5.158.d:
ज्ञातमद्य चला लक्ष्मीस्तेन त्यक्तं सुदूरतः ..
तस्माद्बंधुजनैः सार्धं देवैर्विप्रैश्च कृत्स्नशः ..
संविभक्तां करिष्यामि सत्येनात्मानमालभे .. 6 ..
5.158.m: Today it is known that fortune is fleeting; therefore, it has been cast far away. / Consequently, together with my kinsmen, with the gods and the brahmins entirely, / I shall make it distributed; I swear by truth upon myself!”

5.158.s:
evamuktvā tataḥ sarvānsamāhūya pṛthakpṛthak ..
sa nāmabhirdadau vastraṃ bhūṣaṇāni yathārhataḥ .. 7 ..
5.158.d:
एवमुक्त्वा ततः सर्वान्समाहूय पृथक्पृथक् ..
स नामभिर्ददौ वस्त्रं भूषणानि यथार्हतः .. 7 ..
5.158.m: Having spoken thus, then calling all of them individually, / he gave clothing and ornaments by their names according to their merit.

5.158.s:
tato vedavido viprānsamāhūya sa nāmabhiḥ ..
ekaikasya dadau vittaṃ savastraṃ śraddhayānvitaḥ .. 8 ..
5.158.d:
ततो वेदविदो विप्रान्समाहूय स नामभिः ..
एकैकस्य ददौ वित्तं सवस्त्रं श्रद्धयान्वितः .. 8 ..
5.158.m: Then, summoning the brahmins who know the Vedas by their names, / endowed with faith, he gave wealth along with cloth to each one.

5.158.s:
tatastu nartakebhyaśca dīnāṃdhebhyo viśeṣataḥ ..
dadau bhojyaṃ sami ṣṭānnaṃ savastraṃ ca dvijottamāḥ .. 9 ..
5.158.d:
ततस्तु नर्तकेभ्यश्च दीनांधेभ्यो विशेषतः ..
ददौ भोज्यं समि ष्टान्नं सवस्त्रं च द्विजोत्तमाः .. 9 ..
5.158.m: Then to dancers, and especially to the wretched and the blind, / he gave food, along with sweetmeats and garments, O best of the twice-born.

5.158.s:
tatastu svayamevānnaṃ bubhuje bhāryayā saha ..
visṛjya tānsamāyātānsvajanānbrāhmaṇaiḥ saha .. 6.159.10 ..
5.158.d:
ततस्तु स्वयमेवान्नं बुभुजे भार्यया सह ..
विसृज्य तान्समायातान्स्वजनान्ब्राह्मणैः सह .. 6.159.10 ..
5.158.m: Then he himself partook of food together with his wife, / having dismissed those assembled relatives together with the brahmins.

5.158.s:
evaṃ tena tadā prāptaṃ vittaṃ ca parasaṃbhavam ..
bubhuje svecchayā nityaṃ tadā bhāryāsamanvitaḥ .. 11 ..
5.158.d:
एवं तेन तदा प्राप्तं वित्तं च परसंभवम् ..
बुभुजे स्वेच्छया नित्यं तदा भार्यासमन्वितः .. 11 ..
5.158.m: Thus the wealth originating from another was acquired by him at that time; / accompanied by his wife, he enjoyed it continually according to his pleasure.

5.158.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśīti sāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye puṣpavibhavaprāptivarṇanaṃnāmaikonaṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 159 ..
5.158.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीति साहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये पुष्पविभवप्राप्तिवर्णनंनामैकोनषष्ट्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 159 ..
5.158.m: Thus ends the one hundred fifty-ninth chapter, entitled “Description of Puṣpa's Attainment of Wealth”, in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.159.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
anyasminnahani prāpte rahasyuktaḥ sa bhāryayā ..
rātrau prasuptaḥ pārśve ca pādau saṃspṛśya tatkṣaṇāt .. 1 ..
5.159.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अन्यस्मिन्नहनि प्राप्ते रहस्युक्तः स भार्यया ..
रात्रौ प्रसुप्तः पार्श्वे च पादौ संस्पृश्य तत्क्षणात् .. 1 ..
5.159.m: Sūta said: / When another day arrived, he was spoken to in secret by his wife; / while he was asleep at night beside her, immediately touching his feet, [she said]:

5.159.s:
tvaṃ tāvanmama bharttāsi yāvajjīvamasaṃśayam ..
tadvadasva vibho'smākaṃ tvadarthaṃ sa mayojjhitaḥ .. 2 ..
5.159.d:
त्वं तावन्मम भर्त्तासि यावज्जीवमसंशयम् ..
तद्वदस्व विभोऽस्माकं त्वदर्थं स मयोज्झितः .. 2 ..
5.159.m: “You are indeed my husband for the duration of life, without doubt. / Therefore tell [me], O lord, for your sake that [man] was abandoned by me:

5.159.s:
indrajālamidaṃ kiṃ te kiṃ vā maṃtraprasādhanam ..
devānāṃ vā prasādo'yaṃ yattvaṃ caitādṛśaḥ sthitaḥ .. 3 ..
5.159.d:
इन्द्रजालमिदं किं ते किं वा मंत्रप्रसाधनम् ..
देवानां वा प्रसादोऽयं यत्त्वं चैतादृशः स्थितः .. 3 ..
5.159.m: Is this sorcery of yours, or the accomplishment of a mantra, / or is this the grace of the gods, that you stand in such a form?

5.159.s:
mayā tvaṃ hi tadā jñātaḥ prathame'pi dine sthite ..
yadā saṃbhūṣitā vastraistathā vastuvibhūṣaṇaiḥ .. 4 ..
5.159.d:
मया त्वं हि तदा ज्ञातः प्रथमेऽपि दिने स्थिते ..
यदा संभूषिता वस्त्रैस्तथा वस्तुविभूषणैः .. 4 ..
5.159.m: Indeed, you were recognized by me even when the first day arrived, / when I was adorned with garments and with ornaments of precious things.

5.159.s:
yadyahaṃ tava vārtāṃ ca sarvāṃ kapaṭasaṃbhavām ..
kathayāmi dvitīyasya tatte pādau spṛśāmyaham .. 5 ..
5.159.d:
यद्यहं तव वार्तां च सर्वां कपटसंभवाम् ..
कथयामि द्वितीयस्य तत्ते पादौ स्पृशाम्यहम् .. 5 ..
5.159.m: If I tell your entire tale born of deceit / to another person, then I touch your feet [in false oath]!”

5.159.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evamukto vihasyoccaiḥ sa tadā brāhmaṇottamāḥ ..
tāmāliṃgya tataḥ prāha vacanaṃ madhurākṣaram .. 6 ..
5.159.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्तो विहस्योच्चैः स तदा ब्राह्मणोत्तमाः ..
तामालिंग्य ततः प्राह वचनं मधुराक्षरम् .. 6 ..
5.159.m: Sūta said: / Being addressed thus, laughing aloud, O best of brahmins, / and embracing her, he then spoke words of sweet syllables:

5.159.s:
sādhu priye tvayā jñātaṃ sarvaṃ mama viceṣṭitam ..
ahaṃ sa vipraḥ subhage maṇibhadreṇa yaḥ purā .. 7 ..
5.159.d:
साधु प्रिये त्वया ज्ञातं सर्वं मम विचेष्टितम् ..
अहं स विप्रः सुभगे मणिभद्रेण यः पुरा .. 7 ..
5.159.m: “Well done, my beloved! All my undertaking has been recognized by you. / I am that brahmin, O auspicious one, who formerly by Maṇibhadra

5.159.s:
viḍaṃbito mukhaṃ paśyaṃstvadīyaṃ caṃdrasannibham ..
camatkārapuraṃ gatvā mayā cārādhito raviḥ ..
tena tuṣṭena me dattaṃ tadrūpaṃ jñānameva ca ..8.. ..
5.159.d:
विडंबितो मुखं पश्यंस्त्वदीयं चंद्रसन्निभम् ..
चमत्कारपुरं गत्वा मया चाराधितो रविः ..
तेन तुष्टेन मे दत्तं तद्रूपं ज्ञानमेव च ..8.. ..
5.159.m: was mocked while gazing at your moon-like face. / Having gone to Camatkārapura, the Sun was worshipped by me; / by him, being pleased, that form and knowledge itself were given to me.”
Māhikā said: / “By the sight of you, I have fallen under the power of the god of love.

5.159.s:
tasmādārādhayiṣyāmi taṃ gatvā dinanāyakam ..
yena te tādṛśaṃ bhūyaḥ pratuṣṭo vidadhāti saḥ .. 6.160.10 ..
5.159.d:
तस्मादाराधयिष्यामि तं गत्वा दिननायकम् ..
येन ते तादृशं भूयः प्रतुष्टो विदधाति सः .. 6.160.10 ..
5.159.m: Therefore, having gone, I shall propitiate that lord of the day / so that, greatly pleased, he may again make you like that.

5.159.s:
kiṃ me caitena rūpeṇa tāruṇyenāpi ca prabho ..
yatte tathāvidhaṃ rūpaṃ saṃbhajāmi divāniśam .. 11 ..
5.159.d:
किं मे चैतेन रूपेण तारुण्येनापि च प्रभो ..
यत्ते तथाविधं रूपं संभजामि दिवानिशम् .. 11 ..
5.159.m: What use to me is this [old] form, and even my youth, O master, / unless I constantly enjoy such a form of yours day and night?”

5.159.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tacchrutvā guṭikāṃ puṣpa samādāya mukhāntataḥ ..
dadhāra tādṛśaṃ rūpaṃ yādṛgdṛṣṭaṃ purā tayā .. 12 ..
5.159.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तच्छ्रुत्वा गुटिकां पुष्प समादाय मुखान्ततः ..
दधार तादृशं रूपं यादृग्दृष्टं पुरा तया .. 12 ..
5.159.m: Sūta said: / Hearing that, taking out the pill from within his mouth, / Puṣpa assumed such a form as had been seen by her formerly.

5.159.s:
tataḥ sā harṣitā māhī pulakena samanvitā ..
tamāliṃgyābhajadgāḍhaṃ vākyametaduvāca ha .. 13 ..
5.159.d:
ततः सा हर्षिता माही पुलकेन समन्विता ..
तमालिंग्याभजद्गाढं वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह .. 13 ..
5.159.m: Then Māhī, delighted and accompanied by horripilation, / embracing him, passionately enjoyed him and indeed spoke this word:

5.159.s:
adya me saphalaṃ janma yauvanaṃ rūpameva ca ..
yattvaṃ hṛdvāṃchitaḥ kāṃtaḥ pralabdho madanopamaḥ .. 14 ..
5.159.d:
अद्य मे सफलं जन्म यौवनं रूपमेव च ..
यत्त्वं हृद्वांछितः कांतः प्रलब्धो मदनोपमः .. 14 ..
5.159.m: “Today my birth, youth, and beauty itself have borne fruit, / since you, a beloved desired by my heart and equal to the god of love, have been attained!

5.159.s:
etāvaṃti dinānyeva na mayā kāmajaṃ sukham ..
api svalpataraṃ labdhaṃ kathaṃcidvṛddhasevayā .. 15 ..
5.159.d:
एतावंति दिनान्येव न मया कामजं सुखम् ..
अपि स्वल्पतरं लब्धं कथंचिद्वृद्धसेवया .. 15 ..
5.159.m: For so many days, not even the slightest pleasure born of passion / was obtained by me somehow by serving an old man.

5.159.s: bhajasva svecchayā vipra dāsī te'haṃ vyavasthitā .. 16 ..
5.159.d: भजस्व स्वेच्छया विप्र दासी तेऽहं व्यवस्थिता .. 16 ..
5.159.m: Enjoy [me] according to your pleasure, O brahmin; I stand as your maidservant!”

5.159.s:
.. puṣpa uvāca .. ..
praviśāmi kimaṃgeṣu bhavantīṃ kiṃ milāmyaham ..
priye cireṇa labdhāsi na jāne kara vāṇi kim .. 17 ..
5.159.d:
.. पुष्प उवाच .. ..
प्रविशामि किमंगेषु भवन्तीं किं मिलाम्यहम् ..
प्रिये चिरेण लब्धासि न जाने कर वाणि किम् .. 17 ..
5.159.m: Puṣpa said: / “Shall I enter into your limbs? Shall I blend into you? / O beloved, you are attained after a long time; I do not know what I should do!”

5.159.s:
evamuktvā tatastau ca maithunāya kṛtakṣaṇau ..
pravṛttau brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ kāmadevavaśaṃgatau .. 198 ..
atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāmudite sūryamaṇḍale ..
vaktre tāṃ guṭikāṃ kṛtvā sa puṣpastādṛśo'bhavat .. 19 ..
evaṃ tasya sthitasyātra mahānkālo vyajāyata ..
putrāḥ pautrāstathā jātāḥ kanyakāśca tathaiva ca .. 6.160.20 ..
sa vṛddhatvaṃ yadā prāpto jarāviplavatāṃ gataḥ ..
tadā sa cintayāmāsa mayā pāpaṃ mahatkṛtam .. 21 ..
maṇibhadro varāko'sau mithyācāreṇa ghātitaḥ ..
tasya bhāryā hṛtā caiva prasūtiṃ ca niyojitā .. 22 ..
hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ tasmādgatvā karomya ham ..
puraścaraṇasaṃjñaṃ ca yena śuddhiḥ prajāyate .. 23 ..
evaṃ sa niścayaṃ kṛtvā puṣpaścitte nije tadā ..
asaṃkhyaṃ vittamādāya camatkārapuraṃgataḥ .. .. 24 ..
5.159.d:
एवमुक्त्वा ततस्तौ च मैथुनाय कृतक्षणौ ..
प्रवृत्तौ ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठाः कामदेववशंगतौ .. 198 ..
अथ रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामुदिते सूर्यमण्डले ..
वक्त्रे तां गुटिकां कृत्वा स पुष्पस्तादृशोऽभवत् .. 19 ..
एवं तस्य स्थितस्यात्र महान्कालो व्यजायत ..
पुत्राः पौत्रास्तथा जाताः कन्यकाश्च तथैव च .. 6.160.20 ..
स वृद्धत्वं यदा प्राप्तो जराविप्लवतां गतः ..
तदा स चिन्तयामास मया पापं महत्कृतम् .. 21 ..
मणिभद्रो वराकोऽसौ मिथ्याचारेण घातितः ..
तस्य भार्या हृता चैव प्रसूतिं च नियोजिता .. 22 ..
हाटकेश्वरजं क्षेत्रं तस्माद्गत्वा करोम्य हम् ..
पुरश्चरणसंज्ञं च येन शुद्धिः प्रजायते .. 23 ..
एवं स निश्चयं कृत्वा पुष्पश्चित्ते निजे तदा ..
असंख्यं वित्तमादाय चमत्कारपुरंगतः .. .. 24 ..
5.159.m:
Having spoken thus, both of them, having made the moment for copulation, / proceeded, O best of brahmins, fallen under the power of the god of love.
Now, when the night had passed and the orb of the sun arose, / putting that pill into his mouth, Puṣpa became as [he was before].
Thus, as he remained there, a great time passed by; / sons and grandsons were born, and daughters likewise.
When he reached old age and had fallen into affliction by decrepitude, / then he reflected: “A great sin has been committed by me.
That wretched Maṇibhadra was slain through false conduct, / and his wife was abducted and engaged in childbearing.
Therefore, having gone to the field born of Hāṭakeśvara, / I shall perform what is named puraścaraṇa, whereby purification arises.”
Having thus made a resolve in his own mind, / Puṣpa then, taking boundless wealth, went to Camatkārapura.

5.159.s:
putrebhyo'pi yathāsaṃkhyaṃ dattvā caiva pṛthakpṛthak ..
prāsādaṃ kārayāmāsa tasya sūryasya śobhanam .. 25 ..
yasminsiddhiṃ gataḥ so'tra yājñavalkyapratiṣṭhite ..
tato madhyamamāhūya praṇipatyābhivādya ca ..
so'bravīdbrāhmaṇānāṃ me cātuścaraṇamānaya .. 26 ..
yenāhamagrato bhūtvā prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhaye ..
puraścaraṇasaṃjñaṃ tu prārthayāmi yathāvidhi .. 27 ..
iti skānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṃḍe hāṭa keśvarakṣetramāhātmye puṣpasya pāpakṣālanārthaṃ hāṭakeśvarakṣetragamanapuraścaraṇārthabrāhmaṇāmantraṇavarṇanaṃnāma ṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 160 ..
5.159.d:
पुत्रेभ्योऽपि यथासंख्यं दत्त्वा चैव पृथक्पृथक् ..
प्रासादं कारयामास तस्य सूर्यस्य शोभनम् .. 25 ..
यस्मिन्सिद्धिं गतः सोऽत्र याज्ञवल्क्यप्रतिष्ठिते ..
ततो मध्यममाहूय प्रणिपत्याभिवाद्य च ..
सोऽब्रवीद्ब्राह्मणानां मे चातुश्चरणमानय .. 26 ..
येनाहमग्रतो भूत्वा प्रायश्चित्तं विशुद्धये ..
पुरश्चरणसंज्ञं तु प्रार्थयामि यथाविधि .. 27 ..
इति स्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखंडे हाट केश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये पुष्पस्य पापक्षालनार्थं हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रगमनपुरश्चरणार्थब्राह्मणामन्त्रणवर्णनंनाम षष्ट्यधिकशततमोऽध्यायः .. 160 ..
5.159.m:
And having given to his sons individually according to their number, / he caused a splendid temple to be built for that Sun,
at which temple installed by Yājñavalkya he had attained perfection here. / Then, calling an assembly, having prostrated and greeted [them], / he said: “Bring for me the fourfold assembly of brahmins,
so that, coming before them for complete purification, / I may duly request the expiation called puraścaraṇa.”
Thus ends the one hundred sixtieth chapter, entitled “Description of the Journey to Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra for the Washing Away of Sin and the Inviting of Brahmins for Puraścaraṇa by Puṣpa”, in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.160.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
atha tena dvijāḥ sarve brahmasthāne niveśitāḥ ..
cātuścaraṇasaṃjñāśca tatastasya niveśitāḥ .. 1 ..
5.160.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अथ तेन द्विजाः सर्वे ब्रह्मस्थाने निवेशिताः ..
चातुश्चरणसंज्ञाश्च ततस्तस्य निवेशिताः .. 1 ..
5.160.m: Sūta said: / Then all the twice-born were seated by him in the Brahmasthāna, / and then those called the fourfold assembly were seated for him.

5.160.s:
so'pi keśānparityajya sarvagātrasamudbhavān ..
nijapatnyā samopetaḥ praṇamya ca dvijottamān .. 2 ..
5.160.d:
सोऽपि केशान्परित्यज्य सर्वगात्रसमुद्भवान् ..
निजपत्न्या समोपेतः प्रणम्य च द्विजोत्तमान् .. 2 ..
5.160.m: He too, having discarded the hair growing from all his limbs, / accompanied by his own wife and bowing to the best of the twice-born,

5.160.s:
kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā vākyametaduvāca ha ..
bhāskarasyāsya vihitaḥ prāsādoyaṃ mayā dvijāḥ .. 3 ..
5.160.d:
कृतांजलिपुटो भूत्वा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ..
भास्करस्यास्य विहितः प्रासादोयं मया द्विजाः .. 3 ..
5.160.m:
With folded hands, he spoke these words:
“O twice-born, this temple has been built by me for this Sun.

5.160.s:
puṣpāditya iti khyātiṃ prayātu bhuvanatraye ..
.. brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ .. ..
na vayaṃ yājñavalkyasya kīrtiṃ neṣyāmahe kṣayam .. 4 ..
5.160.d:
पुष्पादित्य इति ख्यातिं प्रयातु भुवनत्रये ..
.. ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः .. ..
न वयं याज्ञवल्क्यस्य कीर्तिं नेष्यामहे क्षयम् .. 4 ..
5.160.m:
May it attain renown in the three worlds as Puṣpāditya.”
The brahmins said:
“We shall not bring to ruin the fame of Yājñavalkya.

5.160.s:
prāyaścittaṃ pradāsyāmaścittasya hṛdayaṃgamam ..
anye ca brāhmaṇāḥ procuḥ kecinmadhyasthavṛttayaḥ .. 5 ..
5.160.d:
प्रायश्चित्तं प्रदास्यामश्चित्तस्य हृदयंगमम् ..
अन्ये च ब्राह्मणाः प्रोचुः केचिन्मध्यस्थवृत्तयः .. 5 ..
5.160.m:
We will grant an expiation pleasing to your heart.”
Other brahmins, adopting an impartial stance, said:

5.160.s:
vṛttyarthamasya devasya lakṣaṃ home'tra kalpyatām ..
lakṣaṃ tu sarvaviprāṇāṃ prāyaścittaviśuddhaye .. 6 ..
5.160.d:
वृत्त्यर्थमस्य देवस्य लक्षं होमेऽत्र कल्प्यताम् ..
लक्षं तु सर्वविप्राणां प्रायश्चित्तविशुद्धये .. 6 ..
5.160.m:
“For the maintenance of this deity, let one hundred thousand [oblations] be appointed in the burnt offering here,
and one hundred thousand [coins] for all the brahmins, for purification through expiation.”

5.160.s:
.. puṣpa uvāca .. ..
tasmātsarve dvijaśreṣṭhā mannāmnā kīrtayaṃtvimam ..
puṣpādityamiti khyātiṃ kīrtayaṃtu tathāniśam .. 7 ..
5.160.d:
.. पुष्प उवाच .. ..
तस्मात्सर्वे द्विजश्रेष्ठा मन्नाम्ना कीर्तयंत्विमम् ..
पुष्पादित्यमिति ख्यातिं कीर्तयंतु तथानिशम् .. 7 ..

5.160.s:
anayā bhāryayā mahyaṃ mānyā yā sthāpitā purā ..
durgā'syāścātra nāmnā vai bhūyātkhyātā'tra satpure .. 8 ..
5.160.d:
अनया भार्यया मह्यं मान्या या स्थापिता पुरा ..
दुर्गाऽस्याश्चात्र नाम्ना वै भूयात्ख्याताऽत्र सत्पुरे .. 8 ..
5.160.m:
And the revered Durgā, who was installed formerly by this wife of mine,
let her also be known by her name here in this noble city.”

5.160.s:
.. brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ .. ..
duḥśīlena purā'kāri prāsādo harasaṃbhavaḥ ..
durvāsaḥsthāpitasyāpi bhavadbhistuṣṭa mānasaiḥ .. 9 ..
5.160.d:
.. ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः .. ..
दुःशीलेन पुराऽकारि प्रासादो हरसंभवः ..
दुर्वासःस्थापितस्यापि भवद्भिस्तुष्ट मानसैः .. 9 ..
5.160.m:
The brahmins said:
“Formerly, Duḥśīla built a temple belonging to Hara,
and with minds pleased by you, you [also rebuilt one] installed by Durvāsas.

5.160.s: tathāpyasya tu dīnasya prāsādaḥ kriyatāṃ dvijāḥ .. 6.161.10 ..
5.160.d: तथाप्यस्य तु दीनस्य प्रासादः क्रियतां द्विजाः .. 6.161.10 ..
5.160.m: Even so, O twice-born, let the temple of this wretched man be provided for.

5.160.s:
nāmamātreṇa devasya duḥśīlena yayā purā ..
anenārādhitaḥ pūrvaṃ svamāṃsaireṣa bhāskaraḥ .. 11 ..
5.160.d:
नाममात्रेण देवस्य दुःशीलेन यया पुरा ..
अनेनाराधितः पूर्वं स्वमांसैरेष भास्करः .. 11 ..
5.160.m:
By the mere name of the deity, as formerly by Duḥśīla,
by this man earlier, this Sun was worshipped with his own flesh.

5.160.s:
tasmānna kṣatirasyātha datte nāmni yathā purā ..
nāmnā māhikayā nāma māhītyeva ca sā bhavet ..12..
5.160.d:
तस्मान्न क्षतिरस्याथ दत्ते नाम्नि यथा पुरा ..
नाम्ना माहिकया नाम माहीत्येव च सा भवेत् ..12..
5.160.m:
Therefore, there is no harm if the name is given as before.
By the name of Māhikā, the name [of the goddess] shall indeed become Māhī.”

5.160.s:
.. sūta uvāca ..
puṣpeṇa dāne datte'tha saṃmatenāgrajanmanām ..
madhyamena kṛtaṃ nāma puṣpāditya iti śrutam .. 13 ..
5.160.d:
.. सूत उवाच ..
पुष्पेण दाने दत्तेऽथ संमतेनाग्रजन्मनाम् ..
मध्यमेन कृतं नाम पुष्पादित्य इति श्रुतम् .. 13 ..
5.160.m:
Sūta said:
When the donation was given by Puṣpa with the consent of the twice-born,
the middle name was made Puṣpāditya, as has been heard.

5.160.s:
tatpatnyā cāpi yā tatra durgā devī dvijottamāḥ ..
nāmnā māhikayā nāma māhītyeva ca sā'bhavat .. 14 ..
5.160.d:
तत्पत्न्या चापि या तत्र दुर्गा देवी द्विजोत्तमाः ..
नाम्ना माहिकया नाम माहीत्येव च साऽभवत् .. 14 ..
5.160.m:
And as for the goddess Durgā there [installed] by his wife, O best of the twice-born,
by the name of Māhikā, she indeed became Māhī.

5.160.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭosmi dvijottamāḥ ..
puṣpā dityo yathā jāto yājñavalkyapratiṣṭhitaḥ .. 15 ..
5.160.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं यत्पृष्टोस्मि द्विजोत्तमाः ..
पुष्पा दित्यो यथा जातो याज्ञवल्क्यप्रतिष्ठितः .. 15 ..
5.160.m:
Sūta said:
All this has been related to you as I was asked, O best of the twice-born,
how [the Sun] consecrated by Yājñavalkya became Puṣpāditya.

5.160.s:
adyāpi kalikāle sa dṛṣṭo bhaktyā sureśvaraḥ ..
nāśayeddinajaṃ pāpaṃ narāṇāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ .. .. 16 ..
5.160.d:
अद्यापि कलिकाले स दृष्टो भक्त्या सुरेश्वरः ..
नाशयेद्दिनजं पापं नराणां नात्र संशयः .. .. 16 ..
5.160.m:
Even today, in the Kali age, when beheld with devotion, that lord of the gods
destroys the sins of men accumulated on that day; of this there is no doubt.

5.160.s:
tathā ca saptamīyukte ravervāre dvijottamāḥ ..
aṣṭottaraśataṃyāvatphalahastaḥ karoti yaḥ ..
pradakṣiṇāṃ ca sadbhaktyā sa labhedvāṃchitaṃ phalam ..17..
5.160.d:
तथा च सप्तमीयुक्ते रवेर्वारे द्विजोत्तमाः ..
अष्टोत्तरशतंयावत्फलहस्तः करोति यः ..
प्रदक्षिणां च सद्भक्त्या स लभेद्वांछितं फलम् ..17..
5.160.m:
Moreover, on a Sunday joined with a seventh lunar day, O best of the twice-born,
whoever, holding a fruit in hand, performs circumambulation
one hundred and eight times with genuine devotion, obtains the desired fruit.

5.160.s:
māhīkāmapi yo durgāṃ nityameva prapaśyati ..
na sa paśyati kaṣṭāni tasminnahani karhicit .. 18 ..
5.160.d:
माहीकामपि यो दुर्गां नित्यमेव प्रपश्यति ..
न स पश्यति कष्टानि तस्मिन्नहनि कर्हिचित् .. 18 ..
5.160.m:
Whoever constantly beholds Durgā Māhīkā
never encounters hardships on that day.

5.160.s:
caitraśuklacaturdaśyāṃ yastāṃ pūjayate naraḥ .
tasya saṃvatsaraṃyāvannāpatsaṃjāyate kvacit .. 19. ..
iti śrīskāṃdemahāpurāṇaekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye puṣpādityamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāmaikaṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 161 ..
5.160.d:
चैत्रशुक्लचतुर्दश्यां यस्तां पूजयते नरः .
तस्य संवत्सरंयावन्नापत्संजायते क्वचित् .. 19. ..
इति श्रीस्कांदेमहापुराणएकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये पुष्पादित्यमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनामैकषष्ट्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 161 ..
5.160.m:
A man who worships her on the fourteenth day of the bright half of Caitra
meets with no misfortune anywhere for an entire year.
Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-first chapter, entitled 'Description of the Glory of Puṣpāditya', in the glory of the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth section of the auspicious Skandapurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
